item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
439
ABPZ20 KNHC 220518
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California, and on Hurricane Polo, located a few hundred miles
south-southeast of Manzanillo, Mexico.

Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
The remnants of Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located several
hundred miles southeast of the Hawaiian Islands, continue to produce
showers and thunderstorms that are gradually becoming better
organized. Environmental conditions are forecast to be conducive for
further development, and a tropical depression is likely to form
during the next day or two while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward or northwestward. Interests in the Hawaiian
Islands should monitor the progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure could form in a few days to the south of the
Gulf of Tehuantepec. Thereafter, environmental conditions appear
favorable for gradual development, and a tropical depression could
form late this week or this weekend while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward, parallel to the coast of
southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was 
located near latitude 14.3 North, longitude 130.3 West. Odalys is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). A turn toward 
the north is expected tonight, followed by a gradual turn toward the 
east-northeast and east through midweek. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some strengthening is forecast during the next couple of days, and 
Odalys is forecast to become a hurricane by mid-week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).

----------------------
None.

-------------

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 220258
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 PM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026
 
Odalys is showing signs of becoming better organized tonight. Recent 
IR imagery depicts a plume of convection with cooling cloud-top 
temperatures near the estimated center of the storm, along with a 
persistent convective banding to its south. The latest Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB was 3.5/55 kt, while objective 
intensity estimates are lower, ranging from 37-49 kt. The initial 
intensity is set at 45 kt for this advisory. 
 
The tropical storm is moving toward the west-northwest and is 
centered between a strong mid-level ridge to the northwest and a 
deepening mid-level trough moving through the southwestern United 
States and the Baja California peninsula. A turn toward the north, 
followed by a sharp turn toward the east-northeast with a slight 
decrease in forward speed, is forecast tonight through Tuesday. An 
east-northeastward to northeastward motion is expected through much 
of the remainder of the week as the aforementioned trough deepens 
and stalls over the far eastern Pacific. The track forecast becomes 
more complicated in the longer range, as some interaction between 
Odalys and Hurricane Polo could occur as it parallels the coast of 
southwestern Mexico. The latest NHC forecast has been adjusted 
slightly to the left of the previous track forecast, and remains 
near the middle of the forecast guidance envelope. 

Decreasing vertical wind shear and warm sea surface temperature will 
support gradual strengthening over the next couple of days, and 
Odalys is forecast to become a hurricane by around 36 h. The 
hurricane is forecast to plateau in intensity around midweek, before 
increasing dry-air entrainment leads to slow weakening this weekend. 
The latest NHC forecast is near the upper end of the intensity 
forecast guidance, and is in close agreement with the HCCA and 
Google DeepMind solutions.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 6A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
1200 AM CST Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...POLO RAPIDLY STRENGTHENS TO A CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE...


SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.7N 102.1W
ABOUT 330 MI...530 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 210 MI...340 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...130 MPH...215 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ESE OR 105 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...955 MB...28.20 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Manzanillo, Mexico.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the southwestern Mexico coast should
continue to monitor the progress of this system as additional
watches and warnings could be necessary today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located 
near latitude 14.7 North, longitude 102.1 West. Polo is moving 
toward the east-southeast near 5 mph (7 km/h). This general motion 
is expected to continue today, with a sharp turn toward the 
northwest and west-northwest anticipated tonight and Wednesday. On 
the forecast track, the core of Polo is expected to be near the 
coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days, although 
forecast to remain offshore.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 130 mph (215 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Polo is a category 4 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Continued rapid intensification 
is forecast over the next day or so, and Polo could become a 
potentially catastrophic Category 5 hurricane today or Wednesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80
miles (130 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 955 mb (28.20 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch
area by early Wednesday. 
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 12 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero and Michoacán through
Thursday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 3 to 6
inches is possible in coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima, and
Jalisco through Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Polo are expected to affect portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Mon Sep 21 2026 
174 
WTPZ42 KNHC 220247
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
900 PM CST Mon Sep 21 2026
 
Polo continues to rapidly intensify (RI) this evening. On 
geostationary satellite, the hurricane's structure is becoming 
increasingly impressive, with the earlier ragged eye clearing out as 
very cold cloud tops (-80 C and below) wrap around. In addition, an 
F17 SSMIS microwave pass at 0105 UTC suggests the earlier eyewall 
replacement cycle (ERC) observed from the NOAA-P3 aircraft has 
completed. Not surprisingly, satellite intensity estimates are 
quickly rising, with the latest subjective Dvorak estimate from TAFB 
up to T5.0/90 kt, with the DMINT estimate associated with that 
recent SSMIS pass at 96 kt. Given the continued improvement of Polo 
on satellite, the initial intensity is being increased to 95 kt for 
this advisory.

The intensifying hurricane continues to move a little south of due 
east, with its estimated motion at 105 degrees at 4 kt. This 
short-term motion is expected to continue for the next 12-18 h 
before mid- to upper-level ridging over Mexico intensifies. The net 
result of this synoptic pattern change is that the primary steering 
should flip in about 24 h, causing Polo to make a sharp turn to the 
northwest and then west-northwest in the 36-60 h time frame, 
bringing the core of the hurricane near, but just offshore of, the 
coast of southwestern Mexico. Finally, toward the end of the 
forecast period, Polo will likely be reaching the westward extent of 
the deep-layer ridge. In addition, Polo may also be approaching 
Tropical Storm Odalys that is forecast to be positioned west of 
Polo, and much of the track guidance responds to this evolution by 
showing the hurricane turning more northward by 120 h. There 
continues to be quite a bit of cross-track uncertainty, both in 
terms of how sharp Polo's turn to the northwest will be in the next 
48 h, and also toward the end of the forecast when Polo could 
experience binary interaction with Odalys. The NHC track forecast 
continues to favor a blend of the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach 
(HCCA) and Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) aids, but the track 
uncertainly remains high in the 3-5 day period. 

Now that it appears the earlier ERC has completed, it is hard to see 
what could prevent Polo from continuing to RI for the next day or 
so. Shear remains low, analyzed at 6 kt by UW-CIMSS, and there is 
ample deep-layer moisture. Sea-surface temperatures are also very 
warm (31 C) and extend vertically down 50-100 meters along the 
short-term track of Polo per a ARGO profiler, which should limit 
cooler ocean upwelling despite the slow motion of the hurricane. 
SHIPS RI indices continue to be very high, with DTOPS showing an 81 
percent chance of at least a 40 kt increase in intensity over the 
next 24 h. Thus, the NHC intensity forecast will continue to show 
RI, and now shows a 140-kt peak in 24 h. This intensity forecast 
agrees with the HCCA intensity aid, and is also close to the 18z 
HAFS-B forecast which also shows a 140-kt peak in its raw output in 
24 h. Beyond that time, inner-core fluctuations related to 
additional ERCs will likely lead to intensity oscillations, and both 
the GFS- and EC-SHIPS guidance does show a marked increase in 
easterly shear beyond 48 h. Therefore, slow weakening is shown in 
the day 3-5 period, though it still remains a bit higher than the 
intensity guidance consensus aside from HCCA. Regardless, Polo is 
expected to remain a major hurricane through the entire forecast 
period.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions
of southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
2. Polo is forecast to strengthen to a major hurricane while it
moves closer to the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few
days. Although the core of the hurricane is forecast to stay
offshore, it is too soon to determine the exact location or
magnitude of impacts. Residents in southwestern Mexico should
closely monitor its progress and updates to the forecast. A Tropical
Storm Watch is in effect for portions of southwestern Mexico and 
has been extended to Manzanillo. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  23/0000Z 15.1N 101.7W  140 KT 160 MPH
 36H  23/1200Z 15.6N 102.2W  140 KT 160 MPH
